context: Reflecting on what keeps democracy alive
purpose: Draw closing lessons; teach 民主/集団/支配/司法/民族/態度/長官

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 民主って、維持するのも大変なんですね。
lines.en: Democracy is hard to maintain too.
lines.style: sobered student reaching a mature point

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 一つの集団が暴走すれば、また支配が生まれます。
lines.en: If one group runs amok, domination returns.
lines.style: teacher delivering a cautionary truth, voice clear and distinctly their own

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: だから司法のチェックが大事なんだ。
lines.style: teen consolidating the lesson firmly, tone holding steady through the whole line

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 多様な民族が共に生きる知恵も問われます。
lines.en: The wisdom for diverse peoples to coexist is tested too.
lines.style: teacher widening the moral scope, delivery emotionally grounded and unforced

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 市民の態度が、社会の質を決めますね。
lines.en: Citizens’ attitudes decide a society’s quality.
lines.style: student articulating civic responsibility, spoken with a recognizable personal cadence

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 長官や大臣も、市民の目で選ばれる時代です。
lines.en: Even directors and ministers are now chosen under citizens’ eyes.
lines.style: teacher closing on accountability, each word carrying genuine natural feeling
